result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.describe()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Print a comprehensive description of the graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.describe()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: Print a comprehensive description of the graph. title: >- [Graph.describe()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: Print a comprehensive description of the graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Print a comprehensive description of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L3472-L3678){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.describe(describe_hook=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Describe](/assets/graphs/describe.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared four-node graph, two triangles sharing the edge B–C, beside the summary describe() prints for it: 4 nodes and 5 edges (both highlighted), undirected, density 0.83, average degree 2.50 ranging from 2 to 3, connected as a single component, and neither a tree nor bipartite." width="100%"} Displays key graph properties including node/edge counts, connectivity, degree statistics, and optional custom properties via a hook function. The summary is printed as aligned `key : value` lines. It always starts with the number of nodes and edges and whether the graph is directed (preceded by the graph's name, if it has one). For a non-empty graph it continues with: - the density and the average, minimum and maximum degree (total degree, i.e., in + out, for directed graphs) - for directed graphs: whether the graph is strongly and weakly connected, and the number of strongly and weakly connected components - for undirected graphs: whether it is connected, the number of connected components, and whether it is a tree and/or bipartite If centrality or other computations have been run on the graph (e.g., by `betweenness_centrality()`), a "Computations" section lists each one with the attribute it wrote and how many nodes have a value. Computations whose result describes the whole graph rather than individual nodes (e.g. `network_robustness()` with the default `return_dict=False`) are listed as "graph-level result (not stored)". Aesthetic mappings created by `colorize_node_attrs()` and `rescale_node_attrs()` are listed in a "Node aesthetics" section. Use `describe()` as a first look at a new or loaded graph, to sanity-check the result of a transformation, or to confirm which computed attributes a graph already carries. Nothing is returned and the graph is not modified. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [describe_hook]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[callable]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A function that takes a Graph as input and returns a dictionary of additional properties to include. Keys are property names, values are the corresponding values to display. The entries are merged into the summary after the built-in properties, so they appear at the end of the main block; a key that matches a built-in property name replaces that value. The hook is called once per `describe()` call. If `None` (default), only the built-in properties are shown. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The description is printed to standard output. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The output is tailored to what the graph actually is: directed graphs surface strong and weak connectivity with their component counts, while undirected graphs report connectivity, the number of connected components, and the tree and bipartite checks. An empty graph only reports its counts and directedness. The built-in statistics include a connectivity analysis and a degree lookup for every node, which is quick for small and medium graphs. Anything the default summary misses, from diameter to a full clustering run, can be layered on via `describe_hook=`. Because that hook is opt-in per call, you can opt into more expensive computations whenever needed and keep routine inspection quick. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Calling `describe()` prints a structured summary to the console. For this undirected three-node path we see the counts, density, degree statistics, and connectivity, along with the fact that it is a tree and bipartite: ::: {#01f5f8f6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C")]) ) graph.describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Number of nodes : 3 Number of edges : 2 Directed : False Density : 0.67 Average degree (min, max) : 1.33 (1, 2) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : True Bipartite : True ``` ::: ::: A directed graph gets strong and weak connectivity instead. In this one, "D" can be reached from the A-B-C cycle but can't get back, so the graph is weakly but not strongly connected. The graph's name is shown first: ::: {#8721798b .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.Graph(directed=True, graph_name="flows").add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), ("C", "D")], auto_create_nodes=True, ) graph.describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Name of Graph : flows Number of nodes : 4 Number of edges : 4 Directed : True Density : 0.33 Average degree (min, max) : 2.00 (1, 3) Strongly connected : False Weakly connected : True Number of strongly connected components : 2 Number of weakly connected components : 1 ``` ::: ::: Pass `describe_hook=` to append your own computed properties to the printout. This is useful for metrics that are too expensive to compute automatically on every call: ::: {#9d91919f .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ec.karate_club() def custom_stats(g): return { "Clustering": g.get_avg_clustering_coefficient(), "Diameter": g.get_diameter() or "N/A" } graph.describe(describe_hook=custom_stats) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Name of Graph : Zachary's Karate Club Number of nodes : 34 Number of edges : 78 Directed : False Density : 0.14 Average degree (min, max) : 4.59 (1, 17) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Clustering : 0.5706384782076823 Diameter : 5 ``` ::: ::: Computations stored on the graph are listed at the end. After computing betweenness centrality, the summary reports the attribute it created and its coverage: ::: {#c04bc7d1 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.betweenness_centrality().describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Name of Graph : Zachary's Karate Club Number of nodes : 34 Number of edges : 78 Directed : False Density : 0.14 Average degree (min, max) : 4.59 (1, 17) Connected : True Number of connected components : 1 Tree : False Bipartite : False Computations: - betweenness_centrality() -> attr: 'betweenness_centrality' (34 of 34 nodes) ``` ::: :::
